rules.rule: Hire date cannot be more than 180 days in the future (DB level, TRG_EMP_BEFORE_INSERT, ORA-20501).
Forms-side hire-date-in-future check uses a 90-day threshold, tighter than the DB's 180-day rule — the two enforcement points disagree.
rules.source: HRMS_EMPLOYEE.xml WHEN-VALIDATE-ITEM (per prior deep-scan; not re-read this pass)

rules.rule: Email must be unique among ACTIVE_FLAG='Y' employees only — a terminated employee's email may be reused by a new hire.
A terminated employee cannot be directly reactivated (EMPLOYMENT_STATUS TERMINATED→ACTIVE is blocked); must go through a separate 'rehire' process instead.
rules.source: TRG_EMP_BEFORE_UPDATE, ORA-20503; corroborated by PKG_EMPLOYEE.rehire_employee existing as a distinct procedure from update_employee

rules.rule: EMPLOYEES rows can never be physically deleted — any DELETE raises ORA-20504; the documented workaround is ACTIVE_FLAG='N' plus Forms CLEAR_RECORD (not DELETE_RECORD).

Salary range per job grade is enforced structurally (MAX_SALARY >= MIN_SALARY) but NOT that an employee's actual salary falls within their job's grade band — PKG_VALIDATION.validate_salary_for_grade exists as a callable check but is not a DB constraint, so it can be bypassed by any path that doesn't call it explicitly.
Leave requires a minimum tenure before it can be taken, per leave type (e.g., FMLA requires 365 days tenure, COMP requires 90 days, PTO/SICK/JURY/BEREAVE require 0).

Leave accrual and carryover rules vary by leave type: PTO accrues 1.25 days/month up to a 20-day max balance with a 5-day carryover expiring after 3 (months, presumed); SICK accrues 0.833 days/month, no expiry on its 10-day carryover; COMP/FMLA/JURY/BEREAVE do not accrue at all (fixed grant model implied).

LEAVE_BALANCES.AVAILABLE formula (canonical): OPENING_BALANCE + ACCRUED - USED + ADJUSTMENT - PENDING. VW_LEAVE_SUMMARY silently uses a different formula omitting PENDING — a business-rule fork, not just a display quirk, since it changes what 'available leave' means depending on which surface an employee/manager looks at.

GOAL_CATEGORY has 5 valid database values (BUSINESS, DEVELOPMENT, LEADERSHIP, INNOVATION, COMPLIANCE) but the Forms UI poplist only allows selecting 3 of them (Business, Development, Leadership) — INNOVATION/COMPLIANCE goals can exist (e.g. from a data load) and display, but cannot be newly assigned through the standard UI.
rules.source: PERFORMANCE_GOALS.CHK_GOAL_CATEGORY vs HRMS_PERFORMANCE.xml poplist (per prior deep-scan)

rules.rule: 'Latest payroll run' is defined as the single highest RUN_ID among APPROVED runs, globally — not per pay-frequency or per employee population, despite the schema supporting REGULAR/SUPPLEMENTAL/BONUS/FINAL run types that could legitimately run in parallel.

Audit retention default is 365 days (PKG_AUDIT.purge_old_records default parameter) — this is a business/compliance rule expressed only as a procedure default, not an enforced scheduled policy (no DBMS_SCHEDULER job found).

Only SALARY_RECORDS, LEAVE_REQUESTS (status changes), and DEPARTMENTS are audited at the DB-trigger level; EMPLOYEES itself (beyond the EMPLOYEE_HISTORY side-channel, which is broken) has no AFTER trigger calling PKG_AUDIT — meaning core employee PII/profile changes are NOT captured in AUDIT_LOG at all, only in the broken EMPLOYEE_HISTORY path.
rules.source: plsql/triggers/trg_audit.sql (only 3 triggers) vs plsql/triggers/trg_employees.sql (BEFORE triggers only, no AFTER/audit call)

rules.rule: Session timeout is a configurable business rule (SYSTEM_PARAMETERS.SESSION_TIMEOUT_MIN = 30 minutes) but is checked against DB server time rather than app server time, per PKG_SECURITY's own documented known-issue — clock skew between DB and Forms app server could cause premature or delayed session expiry.

Password minimum length is a configurable business rule (SYSTEM_PARAMETERS.PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH = 8) but there is no account-lockout-after-failed-attempts rule implemented, per PKG_SECURITY's documented known issues — brute-force protection is a documented gap, not an oversight in this analysis.
Fiscal year starts in month 10 (October) per SYSTEM_PARAMETERS.FISCAL_YEAR_START — relevant to any payroll/reporting logic keyed off fiscal vs. calendar year.

GL (General Ledger) and Benefits external feeds are toggleable via SYSTEM_PARAMETERS (GL_FEED_STATUS, BENEFITS_FEED_STATUS = 'ACTIVE') — implies a kill-switch business control for external integrations, mechanism unconfirmed (PKG_INTEGRATION body unread).
